verses.text: As they came near Jerusalem, they came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two of his followers ahead.
He said to them, "Go to the village in front of you. As soon as you go into it, you will find a young donkey tied there. No one has ever ridden it. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it, and he will send it back here soon.'"
So they went and found a young donkey tied at a door, outside in the street. As they untied it,
some people standing there asked, "What are you doing, untying that donkey?"
They answered as Jesus had told them to, and the people let them go.
They brought the young donkey to Jesus and put their coats over it. Then he sat on it.
Many people spread their coats on the road. Others spread branches they had cut in the fields.
The people who went ahead and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!"
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything. But it was already late, so he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
Far away he saw a fig tree with leaves. He went to see if it had any fruit. When he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, because it was not the season for figs.
Then he said to the tree, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!" And his followers heard him say it.

When they reached Jerusalem, Jesus went into the temple. He began to drive out the people who were buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the benches of the people selling doves.
He would not let anyone carry things through the temple courtyard.
Then he taught them. He said, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it a hiding place for robbers!"
The chief priests and the teachers of the law heard this. They began looking for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, Jesus and his followers left the city.
In the morning, as they walked along, they saw the fig tree. It had dried up from the roots.
Peter remembered what had happened. He said to Jesus, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has dried up!"
"Have faith in God," Jesus answered.

"I tell you for certain, if anyone says to this mountain, 'Go and throw yourself into the sea,' and does not doubt in their heart, but believes that what they say will happen, it will be done for them.
So I tell you, when you pray for anything, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
And when you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive them. Then your Father in heaven will also forgive your sins.
But if you do not forgive, your Father in heaven will not forgive your sins either."
They came again to Jerusalem. While Jesus was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders came to him.
"By what authority are you doing these things?" they asked. "And who gave you the authority to do them?"
Jesus replied, "I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
John's baptism, did it come from heaven, or did it come from people? Tell me!"
They talked about it among themselves. They said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From people'..." They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone believed that John really was a prophet.
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you by what authority I am doing these things either."
